description:
Why: docs/research/string-workloads.md lists 'a growable [i64] output (offset lists, category E/F; the alternative is a two-pass kernel)' as a need below its top three and says it is not ticketed. The bitstring accumulator (defk-cmr) covers bit/byte output of data-dependent length, not typed arrays; today a kernel that produces, say, delimiter offsets or token ids must alloc a worst-case size and return {array, count} (the pattern defk-9p6.21's loader uses), or run twice (count, then fill). That works but over-allocates (worst case can be n elements for an n-byte input) and leaves Elixir to trim with binary_part.

Do not build this speculatively: start when a catalog workload (defk-9p6.21's CSV loader, a tape output for parsers, BPE token ids) measures that the {array, count} or two-pass form costs enough to matter.

Scope when started:
1. Measure the cost of the alternatives on the workload: worst-case alloc + {array, count}, two passes, and the bitstring accumulator with 64-bit segments read back as [i64].
2. If a new construct is worth it: a design that keeps the one rule and Elixir mode (an Elixir meaning, e.g. an append-only accumulator like the bitstring one, `acc = append(acc, v)` returning [i64]), value semantics, bounds checks, max_owned: budget (defk-4b2) and frame cleanup on process death.
3. Compile errors, docs/language.md, and generated docs per docs/agents/generated-docs.md.

Done when: either the measurement shows the existing forms are enough (documented in docs/performance.md and language.md's 'results of unknown length' row), or the construct lands with agreement properties and forced-yield tests.

comments.text: The tape benchmark (defk-9p6.30) is a candidate workload for this: it can use a worst-case alloc + {array, count} today and measure whether that form costs enough to justify this construct. Same for defk-9p6.21.

Closed 2026-10-20: the measurement this ticket waited for is done. defk-9p6.21 (numeric loader) recorded in docs/performance.md that two passes (count, then parse into one alloc) cost 6% of the kernel time for CSV and 11% for JSON, so the loader needs no growable output; defk-9p6.30 (tape) used a worst-case alloc and {array, count} with no cost finding against it. docs/language.md's row for results of unknown length already lists both forms. Reopen if a workload measures the two-pass or {array, count} form above ~20%.

title: Output arrays whose length depends on the data: a growable [i64] (when a workload needs it)
